---
title: "Off-block and in-block times"
description: "How OPDI finds when an aircraft leaves its stand (AOBT) and when it reaches its stand after landing (AIBT), and which stand it used."
---

## In one sentence

`AOBT` (actual off-block time) is when the aircraft starts to move away from
its stand, usually pushed back by a tug, and `AIBT` (actual in-block time) is
when it stops at its stand after landing.

## What it needs

- Reports of the track on the ground at the airport, with positions; most of
  the taxi must be received.
- A passage through a **stand** (a marked parking position for one aircraft)
  in the track: the `entry-parking_position` and `exit-parking_position`
  events of the [airport surface events](surface-events.qmd), from the
  stands drawn in OpenStreetMap.
- The take-off and landing times of the track (`ATOT`, `ALDT`, see
  [Take-off and landing times](take-off-landing.qmd)), which tell the
  departure part of the track from the arrival part, and `line-up` and
  `runway-vacated` where they exist.

## How it is computed

The two sides are computed in the same way, one before the take-off and the
other after the landing.

### Movement on the ground

1. **Reports that may be on the ground.** Only reports flagged on the ground,
   without altitude, or at most 2,000 ft above the airport of their leg are
   read, so the flight itself is never read as movement on the ground.
2. **Ground speed.** About 40% of reports on the airport surface carry no
   position and under 1% a reported ground speed. The reported speed is used
   where it exists. Elsewhere the speed is worked out from the distance
   between a report with a position and the previous report with a position,
   when they are at most 30 s apart, and smoothed over three reports.
3. **Moving or standing.** A report is moving above **2 kt** and standing at
   or below it. A report whose speed is unknown keeps the state of the last
   report whose speed is known. A movement ends at a report that shows the
   aircraft standing, or after more than 300 s without any known speed.
4. A movement counts only when it lasts at least **30 s**; shorter ones are
   noise in the speed.

### Parts of the track

5. The take-off and landing times cut the track into **ground parts**. The
   off-block time is looked for in the part before a take-off, the in-block
   time in the part after a landing. A track that lands, stands and departs
   again gets both. A track that never leaves the ground (no take-off or
   landing time and less than 30 s of reports in flight), such as an airport
   vehicle or a towed aircraft, gets no block time.

### Off-block (`AOBT`)

6. Find the **stand stop**: the last stand passage of the part before the
   take-off that lasts at least **600 s** (a shorter passage after the
   push-back is often where the engines are started).
7. `AOBT` is the start of the first movement that starts at or after the
   entry into that stand and is still going on 30 s later. Without a stand
   stop, it is the start of the first movement of the part.
8. The movement must start from a standstill: the report where it starts is
   at most **30 kt** fast (the flag "on the ground" counts only when no speed
   is known). When the track starts with the aircraft already faster than
   that, the moment it left the stand was not seen and no `AOBT` is given.

### In-block (`AIBT`)

9. Find the stand stop: the first stand passage after the landing that lasts
   at least 600 s, or that lasts until the end of the track.
10. `AIBT` is the end of the movement before the longest stop that overlaps
    that passage (a stop between two movements, or between the last movement
    and the end of the track). Without a stand stop, it is the end of the last
    movement of the part. The movement must end in a standstill, as in step 8.

### Checks and the stand named

11. No block time is given on the runway: an `AOBT` less than 60 s before its
    take-off or between `line-up` and that take-off, or an `AIBT` less than
    60 s after its landing or between that landing and `runway-vacated`.
12. A block time needs a stand passage somewhere in the track. It names a
    stand (and its airport) only from a passage in the same ground part that
    lasts at least 30 s or ends within a minute of the block time: the stand
    of the stand stop, otherwise the passage with the longest stay. A stand
    drawn in OpenStreetMap without a name gives no name.
13. The [plausibility checks](plausibility-checks.qmd) then remove a block
    time placed while the aircraft flies (more than 1,500 ft above the
    airport, faster than 80 kt and no report on the ground within 60 s), an
    `AOBT` at or after the take-off of its own part, and an `AIBT` at or before
    its landing.

## Based on

- **Movement on the ground**: derived in part from the start-of-movement
  rule of the [`traffic`](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2019) library (`StartMoving`): moving
  above 2 kt for at least 30 s, with the speed worked out from positions and
  smoothed over three reports. OPDI also uses the reported speed where there
  is one, and adds the parts of the track, the stand stop and the checks.
  `traffic`'s push-back and parking-position detection is not used.
- **Definitions**: `AOBT` and `AIBT` are the off-block (milestone 15) and
  in-block (milestone 7) times of the [A-CDM Implementation
  Manual](../resources.qmd#ref-acdm-manual); taxi-out time is `ATOT` minus `AOBT` and taxi-in
  time `AIBT` minus `ALDT`, as in ICAO's indicators KPI02 and KPI13
  ([GANP KPI overview](../resources.qmd#ref-ganp-kpi)).
- **Related work**: [Schultz, Rosenow and Olive (2022)](../resources.qmd#ref-schultz-2022) set
  off-block when the aircraft is more than 40 m from its first position on
  the stand, and in-block when within 40 m of its last one.
- **Data**: stands from [OpenStreetMap](../resources.qmd#ref-osm-aeroway), as for the
  [airport surface events](surface-events.qmd).

## What is published

Event types `AOBT` and `AIBT`, with `distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`
(interpolated from the events around them); they have no position and no
altitude. The `info` of `AOBT` holds `stand_exit` (time of the stand exit
used), `stand`, `apt_icao`, and the take-off of its part (`take_off`,
`take_off_method`); that of `AIBT` holds `stand_entry`, `stand`, `apt_icao`,
`landing` and `landing_method` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

The flight list repeats them as `aobt`, `aibt`, `stnd_dep` and `stnd_arr`
(see [Milestone columns of the flight list](flight-list-milestones.qmd)).

## Use cases

- **Taxi-out time**: `ATOT` minus `AOBT` of the same flight, per airport and
  hour; combine with an unimpeded time to estimate additional taxi-out time.
- **Taxi-in time**: `AIBT` minus `ALDT`.
- **Stand use**: how long each stand is occupied between an `AIBT` and the
  next `AOBT` of the same aircraft (`info.stand`).

## Limitations

Often missing, because they need reception on the ground at the stand, and
the off-block time is late when the aircraft is first received already
moving. In-block times sit about a minute after airport records given to the
whole minute. See
[Limitations: block times](../limitations.qmd#lim-block-times).
